hero.headline: Sailing Belongs to Everyone.
hero.subhead: Feel the wind. Take the helm. Discover what you can do.
hero.body:
Based in West Sacramento, West Sacramento Inclusive Sailing Foundation opens the world of sailing to people who have historically faced barriers to the sport.

With adaptive sailboats, experienced support, and safety at the center of everything we do, we make it possible to get on the water, learn to sail, and go as far as your ambition takes you.

home_blocks.headline: Feel the Wind Differently.
home_blocks.body:
There's something powerful about taking the helm of a sailboat.

You're not simply along for the ride. You're reading the wind, making decisions, controlling the boat, and discovering what you're capable of.

Our adaptive sailboats and individualized support help sailors of different abilities participate safely and actively in the sport.

This is sailing. And you can do it.

home_blocks.headline: Your First Sail Could Be Just the Beginning.
home_blocks.body:
Come experience sailing for the first time. Learn to sail independently. Build your skills. Learn to race.

For sailors who want to compete, the opportunities can extend from Northern California to regattas around the world.

You decide how far you want to go.

home_blocks.headline: Everyone can Sail.
home_blocks.body:
Access to sailing takes the right boats, adaptive equipment, skilled instruction, trained support, and a commitment to safety.

Donors and corporate partners make that possible.

Your support gives more people the opportunity to experience the wind, take control of a sailboat, and discover a sport they may never have imagined was open to them.

home_closing.headline: Everyone Can Sail
home_closing.body: For the freedom, for the challenge, for the love of sailing.

sail.headline: Come Sail With Us.
sail.subhead: Feel the wind. Take the helm. Discover what you can do.
sail.intro: Whether you have a disability, have never had access to sailing, or simply never imagined sailing could be for you, there's a way to get on the water.

adaptive.headline: Adaptive Sailing
adaptive.body: Our adaptive sailing program gives people with disabilities the opportunity to learn to sail in adaptive sailboats with experienced support and safety at the center of every experience.
adaptive.getting_started_body:
Adaptive sailors begin by applying through the Challenged Athletes Foundation (CAF).

Once approved, your annual Lake Washington Sailing Club membership is covered by CAF.

To participate, sailors must:
requirements: Be able to transfer safely from the dock into the sailboat or be comfortable with an assisted transfer using our transfer equipment.
Bring a support person who is willing to learn how to rig and de-rig the sailboat and provide an extra set of hands when needed.
adaptive.closing: Once you're a member, you'll have access to Adaptive Sailing Clinics held throughout the year on Mondays and Wednesdays, as well as access to Lake Washington Sailing Club.

access.headline: Want to Learn How to Sail?
access.body:
You don't need to have a disability to have faced barriers to sailing.

Maybe you never grew up around boats. Maybe sailing has always seemed financially or socially out of reach. Maybe you've simply never had the opportunity.

We want to change that.

Sailors seeking greater access to the sport can join through Lake Washington Sailing Club and pay the Club's annual membership fee.

Membership gives you access to Lake Washington Sailing Club and opportunities to get involved, learn, and become part of the sailing community.

membership.headline: Your Membership
membership.body: Membership runs July 1 - June 30, annually. Adaptive Sailors must seek membership for Lake Washington Sailing Club through the Challenged Athlete Foundation. Access sailors are required to join as a member of the Lake Washington Sailing Club and pay the annual fee.

closing.headline: Your First Sail Is Just the Beginning.
closing.body:
Start with getting on the water.

Learn to sail. Build your skills. Learn to race.

For sailors who want to compete, sailing can take you throughout Northern California, across the country, and around the world.

You decide how far you want to go.

videos.headline: See It In Action
videos.intro: A few moments from out on the water.

items.question: Do I need sailing experience?
items.answer: Not at all. You can come to us having never set sail on a sailboat before. We will help you get started, learn at your own pace, and support you in your sailing journey, no matter how far you want to go.

items.question: Can I sail if I have a disability?
items.answer:
Yes. Our adaptive sailboats and sailing programs are designed to make the sport accessible to people with a range of disabilities.

Safety comes first. We'll work with you to understand what assistance or adaptations you may need to get on the water safely and comfortably.

items.question: How do I get into and out of an adaptive sailboat?
items.answer: Sailors need to be able to transfer from the dock into the sailboat. We'll talk with you about the process before you sail so you know what to expect.

items.question: Do I need to bring someone with me?
items.answer: Adaptive sailors must bring a support person who is willing to learn how to rig and de-rig a sailboat and provide an extra set of hands whenever needed. No sailing experience is required for your support person; we will teach them what they need to know.

items.question: How much does it cost to participate?
items.answer: For sailors with disabilities, membership is covered by the Challenged Athletes Foundation (CAF) once your application is approved. Those seeking access to sailing who do not qualify through CAF join directly through Lake Washington Sailing Club and pay the Club's annual membership fee. Membership runs from July 1 through June 30.

items.question: Where and when do you sail?
items.answer:
Our home base is Lake Washington Sailing Club in West Sacramento.

Adaptive and access sailors have access to Adaptive Sailing Clinics throughout the year, which take place Monday and Wednesday weather permitting.

As sailors develop their skills, opportunities to sail and compete can take them throughout Northern California and beyond.

items.question: Can I learn to race?
items.answer:
Absolutely.

You can sail simply because you love being on the water, or you can learn to race and develop your competitive skills.

For sailors who want to pursue competition, sailing can lead to regattas throughout Northern California, across the country, and around the world.

You decide how far you want to go.

about.headline: We Believe Everyone Deserves the Chance to Sail.
about.intro:
West Sacramento Inclusive Sailing Foundation opens the sport of sailing to people who have historically faced barriers to getting on the water.

Through adaptive sailboats, education, support, and a commitment to safety, we give people the opportunity to feel the wind, take the helm, and discover what they can do.

From a first sail to international competition, every sailor should have the opportunity to decide how far they want to go.

mission.headline: Our Mission
mission.body:
Our mission is to bring the sport of sailing to those who might otherwise be excluded due to disability, economic status, background, or other circumstances that make the sport less accessible.

Working alongside Lake Washington Sailing Club and other sailing organizations, we provide opportunities to learn, from an introduction to sailing through advanced skills and elite competition.

founders.headline: Founded by Sailors. Built for More Sailors.
founders.body:
Jim and Kathi Thweatt founded West Sacramento Inclusive Sailing Foundation to open the sport they love to more people.

Based in West Sacramento and serving sailors throughout Northern California and beyond, the Foundation is building opportunities for people to discover sailing, develop their skills, and become part of a larger sailing community.

board.headline: Our Board
board.intro: West Sacramento Inclusive Sailing Foundation is led by a volunteer Board of Directors committed to expanding access to sailing and building a strong, sustainable organization for the future.

jims_story.headline: Jim's Story
jims_story.body:
For Jim Thweatt, the belief that sport can change what's possible is personal.

Jim lost his lower leg at age 17. Rather than stepping away from athletics, he went on to become an elite adaptive skier and built a career helping others discover their own abilities through sport.

Eventually, Jim found sailing.

What began as another way to compete became much more. Sailing offered independence, challenge, strategy, and the unmistakable feeling of being powered by the wind.

Jim went on to compete internationally and became a member of the U.S. Para Sailing Team, representing the United States on the world stage.

But his experience also showed him something else: too many people never get the opportunity to discover sailing in the first place.

The right adaptive sailboat can make a difference. So can knowledgeable instruction, hands-on assistance, a commitment to safety, and simply having someone say, "Yes. You can sail."

That belief is at the heart of the West Sacramento Inclusive Sailing Foundation.

Jim and Kathi want more people to experience what happens when the barriers come down, the sails go up, and you feel the wind in an entirely new way.

Your first sail can change what you believe is possible.

donate.headline: Put More People at the Helm.
donate.intro:
Your support opens the water to people who may never have imagined sailing was possible.

Every sailor needs the right opportunity to begin. For some, that also means an adaptive sailboat, specialized equipment, experienced instruction, hands-on assistance, and a safe environment to learn.

Your support makes all of it possible.

closing.headline: Open the Water.
lines: A first sail can become a new passion.
A sailor can become a competitor.
closing.body: Help make the next first sail possible.

corporate.headline: Become a Corporate Sponsor
corporate.intro: Corporate partners help provide the adaptive sailboats, equipment, instruction, safety, and opportunities that put more sailors on the water. Corporate partners receive year-round brand visibility through our website, events, and communications, with opportunities for recognition on adaptive sailboats, sailing equipment and clinics, connecting your company directly to inclusive sailing in action.

tiers.name: BREEZE
tiers.body: Help provide the equipment, instruction, and support that introduce more people to sailing.

tiers.name: FAIR WINDS
tiers.body: Expand adaptive sailing opportunities and help sailors build their skills, confidence, and independence on the water.

tiers.name: FULL SAIL
tiers.body: Make a leadership investment in adaptive sailboats, expanded programming, and opportunities for sailors to train and compete throughout Northern California and beyond.

contact.headline: Let's Get You Connected.
contact.body:
Want to sail? Volunteer? Support our work? Have a question?

We'd love to hear from you.

West Sacramento Inclusive Sailing Foundation is based in West Sacramento and serves sailors throughout Northern California and beyond.

privacy_policy.headline: Privacy Policy
privacy_policy.intro: This privacy policy addresses how this website located at https://westsacinclusivesailing.org ("This Site") uses personal information.

sections.heading: Collection of Information
sections.body:
We collect personally identifiable information, like names, postal addresses, email addresses, etc., when voluntarily submitted online. The information provided is used to fulfill a specific request. This information is only used to fulfill your specific request unless you give us permission to use it in another manner.

Log data is also collected. Log data is information your browser automatically sends whenever you visit This Site. Log data includes your Internet Protocol address, browser type and settings, the date and time of your request, and how you interacted with the Site.

sections.heading: Cookie/Tracking Technology
sections.body: The Site (powered by West Sacramento Inclusive Sailing Foundation) may use cookie and tracking technology depending on the features offered. Cookie and tracking technology are useful for gathering information such as browser type and operating system, tracking the number of visitors to the Site, and understanding how visitors use the Site. Cookies can also help customize the Site for visitors. Personal information cannot be collected via cookies and other tracking technology, however, if you previously provided personally identifiable information, cookies may be tied to such information. Aggregate cookie and tracking information may be shared with third parties. This site may use Remarketing technology, including but not limited to, Google Ads Remarketing. Remarketing technology, including Google Ads Remarketing, attempts to display ads to you based on the web pages you view by placing a cookie on your web browser. If you wish to see random ads rather than remarketing influenced ads, you can opt out in several ways: • Opt out of Google's use of cookies by visiting Google's Ads Settings. • Opt out of a third-party vendor's use of cookies by visiting the Network Advertising Initiative opt-out page.

sections.heading: Distribution of Information
sections.body:
Personally identifiable information entered on This Site is distributed to the company represented by This Site, in order for the company to fulfill the specific request.

We may share information with governmental agencies or other companies assisting us in fraud prevention or investigation. We may do so when: (1) permitted or required by law; or, (2) trying to protect against or prevent actual or potential fraud or unauthorized transactions; or, (3) investigating fraud which has already taken place. The information is not provided to these companies for marketing purposes.

sections.heading: Commitment to Data Security
sections.body: Your personally identifiable information is kept secure. Only authorized employees, agents and contractors (who have agreed to keep information secure and confidential) have access to this information. All marketing emails and newsletters from this site allow you to opt out of further mailings.

sections.heading: Privacy Contact Information
sections.body: If you have any questions, concerns, or comments about our privacy policy you may contact us using the information below. Email: sheila@westsacinclusivesailing.org.

privacy_policy.closing: West Sacramento Inclusive Sailing Foundation reserves the right to make changes to this policy. Any changes to this policy will be posted.

accessibility_statement.headline: Accessibility Statement
accessibility_statement.body:
West Sacramento Inclusive Sailing Foundation is committed to providing an accessible and inclusive digital experience for all website visitors, regardless of ability or technology.

West Sacramento Inclusive Sailing Foundation strives to ensure that its website is designed and maintained with accessibility in mind and is continually working to improve usability and accessibility for all visitors.

Our goal is for this website to conform substantially with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA standards. However, some content, including certain third-party materials, embedded media, or linked resources, may not fully meet these standards at all times.

If you experience difficulty accessing any part of this website or need assistance navigating the site, please contact us at sheila@westsacinclusivesailing.org. We also welcome feedback regarding the accessibility of our website and suggestions for improvement.
